The lock file holds the SHA-256 hash of the file's content, two spaces, and the path. [sec:lockfile]
The count is fixed in 1.1, and no flag or setting changes it. [sec:remote-retries]
The values table holds the values a placeholder can name. [sec:config-values]
If you edit the file and then run `sablefile check`, it will fail because the check will detect a drift and print a `DRIFT` message. [sec:check-exit-status]
The lock file is how check finds drift, so run sync after each change you intend to keep. [sec:sync-lock-update]
The check exits with status 0 even when files have drifted, so a script cannot detect drift from the exit status in this version. Read the printed lines instead. [sec:check-exit-status]
The check exits with a nonzero exit status when a generated file has drifted. [sec:check-exit-status]
The docs section does not skip the target at docs/build.log. The ignore entry of *.log in sablefile 1.0 does not skip the target at docs/build.log. [sec:ignore-syntax]
The lock file in sablefile 1.1 records each generated file's mode. [sec:lock-mode]

[sec:sync-create-dirs] Folders for targets  
Yes, with `--apply`, sync creates the missing folders before writing the file.
The lock file is kept in `.sablefile/lock.json`. [sec:lock-mode]
The lock file is how check finds drift, so run sync after each change you intend to keep. Commit the lock file with the rest of the project if you use version control. [sec:sync-lock-update]
The --quiet flag on sync is used to suppress the display of the diff output. It does not change the lock file or the sync process. [sec:sync-default]
Yes, sync creates a folder for a target. [sec:sync-create-dirs]

The `--retries` flag changes how often the command retries a failed fetch of a remote template, in place of the default of 5. N is a whole number, and 0 means no retries. The flag applies only to the command it is given to. [sec:retries-flag]

The 2.0 project's old lock file is migrated when a 2.0 command finds an older `sablefile.lock` and no `.sablefile/lock.json`, and it reads the old file and prints a warning that names both files. If the command writes files, it also writes `.sablefile/lock.json` with each entry's SHA-256 hash, and keeps the mode where the old file has one.
The check command does not report the file if it changes. [sec:check-command]
init stops with an error if `sablefile.toml` already exists, so it never overwrites your configuration. [sec:init-command]
The 1.1 lock file does not care about a file's mode. The mode field is described in lock-mode. [sec:lock-mode]
The old `sablefile.lock` file from version 1.1 is not written to the new lock file, so it remains unchanged. [sec:lock-migration]
The 2.0 lock keeps each generated file's mode, as specified in [sec:lock-mode]. When a lock file is migrated from `sablefile.lock`, the mode is kept where the old file had one. [sec:lock-migration]

The `--retries` flag sets how many times `sync` and `diff` retry a failed fetch of a remote template, in place of the default of 5. Use it on a slow or unreliable network, where a higher count gives the server more chances to answer. [sec:retries-flag]

Check does not see changes on a remote template's server. A change on the server affects what the next sync writes and what diff shows, but check does not fetch anything and never retries. [sec:remote-templates]

The check prints `DRIFT` and the path, and exits with status 1. A check with no drift exits with status 0. Pass `--no-fail` to exit with status 0 even when files have drifted; see no-fail-flag. If check itself cannot run, for example because the lock file cannot be read, it prints an error message.
The mode that sablefile 1.1 stores for each generated file is described in [sec:lock-mode]. The command that stores it is `sablefile lock`. [sec:lock-mode]
The 2.0 lock file JSON contains keys: `lock.json`.
The usual way to preview sync's changes in 1.0 before writing is to use `sablefile diff`. [sec:diff-command]

The lockfile is `sablefile.lock` in the project root. It holds one line for each generated file: the SHA-256 hash of the file's content, then the file's mode, then the path. sync writes it, and check reads it. The mode field is described in lock-mode. The ignore file, `.sablefileignore`, sits in the project root and lists paths that sablefile must leave alone.

Template files are ordinary text files, and they can sit in any folder of the project. The `template` key in a `[[file]]` table gives the path from the project folder. Keep templates under version control with the rest of the project.
The exit status for sync in 1.0 when a template file is missing is 1. [sec:sync-exit-status]
The ignore file, `.sablefileignore`, sits in the project root and lists paths that sablefile must leave alone. A project without an ignore file ignores nothing.
Run `sablefile diff` to see how the file differs from its template. [sec:check-command]

The difference between a placeholder and a value in sablefile 1.0 is that a placeholder is a name in a template that sync replaces with a value, and a value is a string in the `[values]` table of the config file.
The double-star pattern does not work in a sablefile 1.0 ignore file. [sec:ignore-recursive]
The script will fail because the exit status indicates that the drift has occurred. [sec:check-exit-status]
The number of retries for a remote fetch is fixed in 1.1 and does not change. [sec:remote-retries]
The `--retries` flag can be used to set the number of retries for `sync` and `diff` when a remote fetch fails. [sec:retries-flag]
The check will still report DRIFT for the template if the change was made after the last sync. [sec:drift-meaning]
The `--no-fail` flag can be used to stop check from failing when files have drifted. [sec:no-fail-flag]
The file called `sablefile.lock` is not present in 2.0. The docs don't say.
The plan shows the target's content if the folder does not exist yet. [sec:apply-flag]
The [values] table maps names to strings. A number can be used as a bare value. [sec:glossary-terms]
The targets that were not written yet are not affected by the failure. [sec:config-files-table]
The `--retries 0` flag sets no retries for `sync` in 2.0. [sec:retries-flag]
The exit status for sync is 1. [sec:sync-exit-status]
The file in 1.0 that decides which templates sablefile renders is the `[[file]]` table. Each file is listed in the order of the `[[file]]` tables. [sec:diff-scope]
A trailing slash matches a file. [sec:ignore-syntax]
The syntax of ignore entries in 1.0 does not include an ! at the start of the line. The `!` is not available in 1.0. [sec:ignore-syntax]
The ignore file, `.sablefileignore`, is located in the project root and is called the ignore file. The syntax of each entry depends on the version; see ignore-syntax.
